candidates.title: Rdq: does a robot dataset's licence match its source? (checked 3,000 LeRobot datasets)
candidates.summary:
Most LeRobot datasets on the Hub don’t have a licence anyone actually chose. I scanned the 3,000 most-downloaded LeRobot datasets: 56.5% carry apache-2.0 on an untouched template card, which is just push_to_hub’s default.

305 of them can be matched to one of 65 public robot datasets whose terms I checked at the source (DROID, BridgeData, LIBERO, Open X-Embodiment components, …). 201 of those, about a third of all LeRobot downloads, declare a different licence than the original, mostly CC BY 4.0 data relabelled apache-2.0 or mit.

candidates.title: ggml-org/llama.cpp release: b11576
candidates.summary: <details open> graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256 (#30416) The no-cache path builds a [n_tokens, n_tokens] mask and passes K and V unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token) disables flash attention for such models. Pad the mask like llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv and pad K and V with zeros up to the KV dimension of the mask. clef builds its own causal mask and pads it the same way. </details> **Website:**
